Thanks for the ping — I pulled the ICS and inspected the TZ block. Two likely culprits:

1) The original invite used TZID: Europe/Paris (CET) and a mail gateway that rewrites iCal bodies sometimes strips the textual TZ mapping and leaves only a floating local time. When that happens, some clients treat the time as wall-clock local and re-assign it using their default zone (SGT) but without the original offset, which can result in a two-hour shift depending on DST.

2) A second possibility is our calendar tool exported the RRULE/DTSTAMP in UTC but labelled the DTSTART without TZID; some clients (especially older mobile clients or proprietary forwarding services) then display it incorrectly.

Quick mitigation: resend a new invite with DTSTART in UTC and include a full VTIMEZONE block for Europe/Paris and Asia/Singapore, and also pin a SUMMARY line like "DTSTART;TZID=UTC:20270825T120000Z (14:00 CET / 20:00 SGT)" in the body for clarity. That avoids relying on the recipient client to translate correctly.

Proposed slots (converted to all TZs):
- Aug 25 14:00 CET / 13:00 BST / 20:00 SGT (recommended)
- Aug 26 09:00 CET / 08:00 BST / 15:00 SGT
- Aug 27 16:00 CET / 15:00 BST / 23:00 SGT (not ideal)

I can recreate the ICS and send it to Sophie/Tom from an APAC-aware calendar export. Ben — can you hold Aug 25 14:00 CET on your calendar just in case?
